text.title: Poetry Project Setup — Decision Tree
text.summary: Routes on the two questions that actually decide this methodology: is Poetry mandated at all (versus uv), and can CI carry it. Every conclusion references a rule id from 01-core-rules.xml.

decision-tree.root-question: Is Poetry mandated for this project — corporate standard, legacy infrastructure, or an existing Poetry 1.x repo being migrated — rather than freely chosen?

branch.question: Can CI install Poetry and cache `.venv`, and is the project already on PEP 621 with a committed lockfile?

branch.conclusion: Apply the full methodology: PEP 621 as the source of truth, then walk content/04-procedure.xml end to end.
Fix the foundation first — commit `poetry.lock` and migrate metadata into the `[project]` table. The CI and Docker rules are unenforceable until the lockfile is authoritative.
Partial application: get `snok/install-poetry` plus a `.venv` cache keyed on the lockfile hash into CI before adopting the rest, otherwise every rule here is enforced only on developer machines.
Skip: a greenfield project with a free choice should use uv — route to `[[python-modern-2026]]`. A single-file script needs no dep manager at all.

example.p: Legacy corporate repo on Poetry 1.x, GitHub Actions available, no lockfile committed - poetry_mandated=true, ci_supports_poetry=true, pep621_and_lockfile=false - commit the lockfile and migrate to PEP 621 before anything else.
